14. As it will appear from the above observation of the learned Chief Justice of the High Court of West Pakistan, Dacca High Court has consistently taken the view in favour of giving interpretation to the word 'case' and its power to deal with interlocutory orders the revision has seldom been questioned if it has otherwise come within the purview of section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The jurisdiction has been assumed in most cases. In the case of the Hanover Fire Insurance Company Vs. Maralidahr Banechand and others, reported in 8 DLR 186, a Division Bench of the Dacca High Court, in dealing with a question relating to issue of Commissioner for examining a witness living in a foreign country, took the view that when a Court directed issue of the Commission under Order 26, rule 5 of the Code of Civil Procedure, such an order could not be interfered with in revision. As against the said decision, an appeal was preferred to the Supreme Court of Pakistan which reversed the decision of the High Court and took the view in the case reported as Hanover Fire Insurance Company Vs. Messrs. Muriidhar Banechaud in 10 DLR (SC) 136, same case PLD 1958 (SC) 138 that such and could be interfered .within revision. In the said case the trial court directed a commission to be issued for examining a witness resident in India with which country Pakistan had no reciprocal arrangement. for execution of a commission issued by a Civil Court. The High Court, being moved under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure declined to interfere with the said order, but the Supreme Court took the view that in the circumstances of the case, the High Court should have set aside the order of the trial Court and observed as follows:— 

 16. In another case reported as the Levant Shipping Company Vs. Pakistan in (1960) 12 DLR (SC) 129 —P.L.D. 1960 S.C. (Pak) 341, the Supreme Court of Pakistan interfered with an order of the High Court on the same view of the matter. In the said case the Subordinate Judge refused to issue a letter of request for examination of a witness in a foreign country on the ground that there was no reciprocal arrangement. The decision of the learned Subordinate Judge was upheld by the High Court in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction. But, on appeal the Supreme Court reversed the decisions of the learned Subordinate Judge and the High Court and directed issue of letter of request.
